data: Performance Practicum - “This is how we Perform Today”

The journey of performing traditions (dance, music and theatrical performances) into the 20th century is pregnant with its immediate cultural memory. This course will focus on embodied learnings of some of the traditions that have been altered because of the post-colonial censuring that led to a normative establishment of artistic traditions as “classical” and “folk”. Through the course, students will encounter art practices such as Lavani, Gujjili poetry, Karakattam/Kattai Koothu, Raaja paat or  Stri Paat theatre performance and Reality show performances. Through media- embodiment, we will gain foundational knowledge of these forms even as we draw attention to notions of “purity” and “honour” attached to artistic traditions that affect the way we have inherited them. The course uses corporeality in practice as a tool to encounter the socio-political and economic lives of the artistes who practice these arts.
The course does not require the student to have prior knowledge in any art form, but must be willing to participate in class practicums. Grading will be commensurate with willingness and enthusiasm to experiment and learn, rather than expertise in practice. This course is meant to offer further insights towards the Pathways in the Arts course by way of lending an experiential understanding of artistic traditions. The classes will be a mix of embodied learnings (music, dance and theatre forms), video footage viewings and some discussions on performative traditions.
Learning Outcome
Students will learn a range of performative forms, in practice
Students will learn to pause and analyse the nuances of technique in footwork, movements, dialogue delivery and rhythms in each section
They will develop a language of movements  and also learn of the history and politics of embodied performance
